notes: Spent clicks on repeated HQ runs and tag removal while never contesting the remote, where the Corp scored four agendas almost unopposed. No breakers until turn 7, and the late Bravado R&D facecheck ignored an advanced card in Server 2 the turn before the Corp won.

Lost Fujii early from a one-ice remote, then spent several mid-game turns clicking for credits at 9-14 credits and advanced an already-exposed Urtica Cipher. Recovered with sensible single-remote scoring against a passive Runner.

Clicked for credits nearly every turn up to 41 credits, never built a working rig and never ran HQ or R&D. Each scoring remote got one bounce-off run and the Corp scored four agendas behind single ice.

Left R&D unprotected for four turns while the Runner ran it every click, clicking for credits and drawing instead of icing it, which lost two agendas. The later game was solid: Ansel on HQ, Architect Deployment Test, a Seamless Launch fast-advance and a clean close.

Aggressive and effective: stole from the remote early, used Docklands Pass and Maintenance Access well on an agenda-heavy HQ, and won on turn 5. The minor waste was a 0-credit Concerto run into a Loot Box it could not pay for.

Installed Megaprix behind unrezzed ice with 0 credits, so it could not rez and lost the agenda, and later put Ingatan behind a single known Ablative Barrier. Spent most turns near 0 credits from over-installing campaigns, with weak R&D ice and an ice install on an empty server.
Coherent R&D lock: found Nanuq through Rigging Up and kept running R&D to win. Small mistakes included a broke second HQ run through F2P that bounced Gauss and ignoring tags for a long time.

After turn 2 the Runner almost only clicked for credits, reaching 76, and never installed anything or contested a remote. It also paid 13 credits to Measured Response, and the Corp scored four agendas unopposed.

Played Neurospike for no effect, then used Longevity Serum to trash its entire hand and fell to 0 cards and 2 credits. From there it could not rez R&D ice or protect the Lotus Haze reinstalled by Hybrid Release, and the Runner took both.
Never installed ice on HQ, clicking for credits and drawing while holding a hand full of agendas and 7-9 credits. The Runner took four agendas from an open HQ and won on turn 3.

Had about 15 turns against a Runner that only clicked for credits but scored just two Post-Truth Dividends, mostly clicking for credits at 10-15 credits and advancing Vladisibirsk. It discarded Tomorrow's Headline to Archives, where it was stolen, and installed Embedded Reporting twice behind the same lone Grubber.

Built a sensible Banner and Leech plan to keep pressure on R&D through Akhet, but stayed very poor for many turns and ignored HQ for most of the game. At 6 points it clicked for credits for two turns instead of running before winning from Archives.

Gave two tags with Public Trail and never punished them, and protected Next Big Thing with Tsarevna and Ping, which a Mayfly got through. At 6-2 down it then installed Embedded Reporting in the same server the Runner had just breached, which lost the game.
Used Transfer of Wealth to cripple the Corp's credits, then ran R&D repeatedly and won on turn 3. There was too little play to judge further.

Against a Jinteki net-damage deck it kept running unknown remotes with a tiny grip, ate Urtica, Mavirus and a full Karunā instead of jacking out. It was flatlined by stealing Fujii with one card in hand, a foreseeable risk.

Kept an agenda-flooded HQ behind a single Vertigo the Runner broke for 1 credit every run. Meanwhile it banked up to 31 credits clicking and never added HQ ice or installed agendas in a remote, and lost four agendas from HQ.

Early R&D pressure was good and its later willingness to eat Hammer to keep digging R&D won the game. It also installed a second Buzzsaw on turn 1 that wiped out its credits and wasted several turns clicking for credits.

Protected its scoring remote with only Phoneutria, which never ends the run, and the Runner walked in to steal Sericulture Expansion. It then put Fujii in the same server next turn, losing it too, and the game ended on turn 4.

The early game was weak: it clicked for credits and lost Superconducting Hub behind Vertigo and Drafter, which have no end-the-run subroutine. The late game was solid, with Seamless Launch and Architect Deployment Test chains and a revealed Méliès the Runner could not afford to steal, though it wandered between scoring targets.
Banked 40 credits clicking and never installed a breaker. With 34 credits it declined to pay 1 credit to get past Paywall in front of a Kingmaking that was then scored for the win.
